lines: A generative sequencer: it invents a melody, loops it, changes it a little as it goes, and after a while throws it away and invents another
Sets how many steps of the melody are played before it loops, 1 to 32; a full 32-step melody stays in memory whatever this is set to
Picks the scale new melodies are drawn from: Major, Natural Minor, Harmonic Minor, Major Pentatonic, Minor Pentatonic, Dorian, Mixolydian, Chromatic, Tuning, Bhairavi and Ahir Bhairav
Sets how many loops go by before a new melody becomes likely, 1 to 50; at that count the chance of a new melody each loop has reached 50%
Sets the gate length as a share of the average time between clocks, a twentieth of it at the far left and all of it at the far right
Sets what share of the steps carry a note rather than a rest, 0.5% to 100%
Sets the chance that the melody is moved by an octave between loops, 0 to 100%
Sets the chance that single notes are changed between loops, 0 to 100%
Throws away the current melody and generates a new one straight away
Chooses how much may change: new melodies and note changes, note changes with the melody held, or nothing at all
Sets how far an octave move may reach: no move, one octave either way, or two octaves either way
Adds to the length knob, three steps per volt, the total held between 1 and 32
A rising edge past 2V moves the mode switch, in the way the Lock CV In Behavior menu item sets
Adds to the lambda knob, five loops per volt, counted in whole volts only
Adds to the gate knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel
Adds to the density knob, ten percentage points per volt
Adds to the octave chance knob, ten percentage points per volt
Adds to the note change knob, ten percentage points per volt
A rising edge past 2V throws away the current melody and generates a new one
Advances the sequence one step on each rising edge past 2V
A rising edge past 2V sends the sequence back to its first step
The pitch of the step being played, a volt per octave
A 10V gate on every step that carries a note, its length set by the GATE knob
Note — nothing plays until a clock is patched; the module has no clock of its own
Note — the four lamps step along with the sequence and grow brighter as a new melody becomes more likely; the small lamp at the top right lights when a pX is placed immediately to the right
Menu — Mutation can tranpose notes by octave: Off, On — lets a changed note be moved to a different octave as well, within the reach the RANGE switch sets
Menu — Lock CV In Behavior: 0-2, 0-1, 0-1-2, Hi/Low — sets what a trigger at LOCK does to the mode switch; Hi/Low holds everything locked while the jack is high

Proteus.notes: The CV scalings are all in process() at Proteus.cpp:370-385 and none of them is a volt per unit: length moves three steps per volt because maxSteps/10 is integer division, lambda is cast to int before scaling so it only responds in whole volts, and density, octave and mutate each move ten percentage points per volt. The gate knob is configured from 0.05 but the clamp after the CV sum has a floor of 0.1, so the shortest gate reachable with any CV patched is a tenth of the clock gap, and no gate is ever shorter than 10ms (line 518). The source comment beside mode 1 at line 419 says "allow to regen but no mutations", which is the wrong way round: that setting sets mutate true and accumulate false, so note changes carry on and new melodies stop, as the maker's README says.

Jawari.notes: The two pitch jacks are clamped to between -1V and +2V at Jawari.cpp:163-164, so the instrument only transposes over three octaves however far the cable goes, and they are read inside doStep() rather than in process(), which is why a pitch change is only taken up at the next strum. The bridge CV at line 261 is added to the slider without any scaling, so a single volt sweeps the whole control rather than the ten volts the rest of the plugin uses. The strings are Karplus-Strong plucks with a comb filter alongside, mixed by the bridge control, and the output is run through a DC blocker and a gain compensation at lines 299-304.

ProteusX.notes: The module declares two outputs in its OutputId enum but adds no jack for either, so neither can be reached and neither gets a line. None of the five inputs is given a name with configInput, so hovering them shows nothing. The transpose and rest CVs are scaled so that one volt covers the whole control (ProteusX.cpp:448-449), not the ten volts used elsewhere in the plugin. At ProteusX.cpp:443-445 the save, load and clear buttons of a slot are all passed through the same SchmittTrigger, buttonTrigs[button], one after another in the same sample, so the three share one piece of edge-detection state; that is worth testing in the rack before relying on rapid presses.

Raga.notes: The taraf strum jack is configured as "Taraf string tuning" at Raga.cpp:240 but is read at line 666 as a trigger that strums the tarafs; the panel prints TARAF STRUM over it and the code agrees with the panel. The three tuning knobs are configured 1 to 11 (lines 254-260) against note tables holding twelve entries, so the last name in each table, B on the main knob and Ni on the second and third, cannot be selected. The module declares a right-hand audio output in its OutputId enum but adds no jack for it, so the instrument is mono and the second output can never be reached. GLIDETYPE_PARAM is configured at line 252 and read at line 649 but has no widget, so its linear-or-logarithmic choice is fixed at the default and cannot be changed from the panel. The fader sums at lines 633-638 clamp the knob and the CV separately but not the total, so a level above one is reachable.
